text:
Vanessa Ortiz: Heads up for Dedicated throughput tiers work — current shape availability is getting tight again. We need to be explicit in the tier docs about *which regions actually have inventory* (esp Premium).

Irene Choi: +1. Can we get a quick snapshot for H100/A100/L4 by region? PM is asking what we can safely "guarantee" without having Sales over-promise.

capacity-bot: Fleet snapshot (approx, subject to change):
- us-east1: H100 80GB (low), A100 80GB (medium), L4 (high)
- us-west2: H100 80GB (medium), A100 80GB (medium), L4 (high)
- eu-central1: H100 80GB (very low), A100 80GB (low), L4 (medium)
- eu-west1: H100 80GB (none), A100 80GB (low), L4 (medium)
- ap-southeast1: H100 80GB (none), A100 80GB (very low), L4 (low)

Harish Reddy: This matches ops reality. H100 is basically "by exception" outside US right now. Even in us-east1 we’re fighting batch jobs + other reserved pools. Lead time for net-new H100 capacity still ~6–10 weeks depending on vendor.

Jamal Pierce: For Premium tier: we should probably restrict to us-west2 + us-east1 only, and even then require a minimum commit / advance notice. Otherwise we’ll end up doing emergency reshuffles.

Lauren Bishop: That’s helpful. For the tier matrix we were assuming Premium = H100-only. Is that still the right mapping, or do we want Premium to be "H100 preferred" with a fallback to A100 80GB?

Irene Choi: From fleet POV: if Premium includes A100 as a fallback, it needs to be super clear it’s a different baseline/throughput profile. Otherwise we’ll get hammered on "you sold me Premium".

Rafael Mendes: SRE angle: whatever we call Premium, the SLO is only enforceable if the underlying shape is stable. If we allow shape swaps (H100 -> A100) during supply events, we should classify that as a planned change w/ notice, not an incident.

Vanessa Ortiz: Re: A100 fallback — also note a lot of our A100 availability is MIG’d today. If Premium requires no-MIG (for perf consistency / fewer noisy neighbor issues), that shrinks the pool a lot.

Harish Reddy: Yep. Operationally:
- H100: we can keep "no-MIG" as default, but inventory is scarce.
- A100 80GB: large chunk is partitioned for other workloads; converting from MIG -> full GPU is doable but not instant + impacts other commitments.
If Premium requires no-MIG + strict latency guardrails, we should hard-limit region list and gate new deals.

Jamal Pierce: Proposal for docs (happy to be overruled):
1) Premium tier only on shapes: `h100-80gb-x8` (single node) and `h100-80gb-x16` (2-node w/ NVLink only where supported).
2) Regions: US only for now (us-west2 "preferred", us-east1 "limited"). EU/APAC = "contact us" w/ explicit lead times.
3) No MIG for Premium. Performance tier can be either (depending on shape), Standard can be MIG.

Irene Choi: +1 on region allowlist. Also please add a note that Premium capacity is "reserved" only — no burst beyond reserved unless we explicitly confirm spare GPUs in-region.

Lauren Bishop: On burst — we’re drafting tier semantics where Premium has higher burst headroom. If we can’t reliably do that due to supply, should we define burst as "best effort" with throttling allowed?

Rafael Mendes: Please. Define burst as "opportunistic" and explicitly say throttling during burst is *expected behavior*, not an SLO breach. Otherwise oncall gets paged every time someone tries to 3x their reserved concurrency.

Vanessa Ortiz: Also worth calling out the regional constraints with plain language: "Premium may be unavailable in certain regions due to GPU supply". Sales will hate it but it’s better than renegotiating after signature.

Harish Reddy: One more ops note: us-east1 H100 pool has more maintenance churn (vendor swaps). us-west2 has been steadier. If we need a single "recommended" region for Premium, pick us-west2.

Irene Choi: Cool. I’ll summarize as: Premium = US-only initially, H100-only shapes, no MIG, burst is best-effort/opportunistic. I’ll send to Lauren + add to the shape catalog page. (reactions: :thumbsup: x4)

Lauren Bishop: Thanks all. This directly feeds the tier definitions + contract carve-outs (availability by region). I’ll reflect this in the next PRD draft and flag that EU Premium is not GA. (reactions: :white_check_mark: x2)
